questions.title: Split work into balanced ranges
questions.prompt: Return exactly workers half-open index ranges covering [0,n), with no overlap. Earlier ranges receive any extra elements. Their lengths differ by at most one. Empty ranges are allowed. Throw std::invalid_argument when workers is zero. Tests use at most eight workers.

tests.label: Remainder first
tests.hint: Give one extra item to each of the first n%workers ranges.

tests.label: More workers than items
tests.hint: Keep all requested ranges, including empty ones.

tests.label: No items
tests.hint: Empty work still has two empty ranges.

hints: Use n/workers for the shared base length.
The end of one range is the beginning of the next.
questions.explanation: Balanced, nonoverlapping half-open ranges are a useful starting contract for parallel writes. This exercise calculates the ranges; it does not launch GPU or CPU work.

questions.title: Join two CPU tasks before returning
questions.prompt: Split the vector at its middle. Launch two std::async tasks with std::launch::async, each returning its own long long subtotal. Wait for both and return their sum. Keep the borrowed vector alive until both finish. Tests check totals; review your code to verify that it uses two tasks and disjoint ranges.

tests.label: Odd length
tests.hint: The second range includes the remaining item.

tests.label: Wider accumulator
tests.hint: Accumulate in long long, not int.

hints: Each task should own its subtotal instead of sharing one writable total.
future.get waits for completion and retrieves the returned subtotal.
questions.explanation: The tasks share only read access to the vector. Their totals are separate local values, and get establishes completion before the results are combined. Passing these fixtures does not prove a speedup or every concurrency property.

questions.title: Count missed deadlines
questions.prompt: Compare completion times with matching deadlines. A completion exactly at its deadline is on time. Return the number with completion > deadline. Both vectors contain nonnegative integer times. Throw std::invalid_argument if their lengths differ.
questions.signature: std::size_t deadlineMisses(const std::vector<int>& completed, const std::vector<int>& deadlines)
hints: Check equal sizes before the loop.
Use > rather than >= for the late test.
questions.explanation: This checks recorded timing data. It models deadline accounting and makes no claim about real-time scheduling guarantees of the machine running it.
